text: Writing clean code is a crucial skill for any programmer, and it is much more about the human reader than the computer. The main goal is to make code readable and easy to understand, so that others—or even your future self—can work with it without frustration. Using clear naming conventions is the first step; variables like `totalPrice` or `userEmail` are far better than `x` or `data`. Furthermore, breaking a large problem into small, focused functions makes the logic simple to follow. Each function should do one thing well. Ultimately, this effort leads to better maintainability, meaning the code is cheaper to fix, update, and improve over the long term.
